transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~41 minutes
Attendees: Laura (Redwood AE), Ravi (CSM), Maya (SE) — Jonas, Aisha, Tom (Pelican)

Summary: quick activation kickoff focused on observability, network/VPC intake, SSO/SAML, and a lightweight latency/cost profile so we can scope the Dedicated trial. Customer emphasized compliance posture and desire for token-level cost visibility.

00:00 Laura (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time, i'll kick off — quick intros, then go into the runbook items and what we need from pelican to get a Dedicated/Private trial up.
00:14 Jonas (Pelican): yeah thanks, appreciate it. we just want to make sure this is low friction — our SRE team needs the observability hooks and sso to be in place before we send anything prod-ish.
00:28 Maya (Redwood SE): cool, i can take observability questions. brief note — we have token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards in the console, i'll demo if we have time but also can follow up with a focused session.
00:44 Aisha (SRE): perfect. i also want to understand batching and caching because our traffic is spiky — some hourly bursts, some steady. what's the common pattern you see?
00:58 Maya: typically we recommend prefix/KV caching for prompt-heavy flows, and continuous batching for stable low-latency paths. for bursty workloads we suggest a small dedicated pool with burst capacity — that keeps p95 low while saving unit cost on steady traffic.
01:15 Tom (Security): can you clarify encryption at rest — we need KMS integration and HSM for certain keys. also SOC2 status?
01:26 Laura: good questions. we are SOC2 compliant; for Private deployments we can surface customer-managed KMS (we integrate with common cloud KMS and have options for HSM). i'll attach the security pack after the call.
01:42 Jonas: great. on networking — we're on GCP with a VPC that peers to our tenant VPCs. how intrusive is the networking setup?
01:54 Ravi (CSM): it depends on Dedicated vs Private. for Dedicated we provide a peering/VPN option and a minimal set of CIDR rules plus an ingress/egress checklist. for Private (VPC-hosted) there's a little more setup since control plane traffic also needs to be considered. we'll send the network diagram template.
02:13 Aisha: okay send that; also, do you support private subnets only (no internet egress)?
02:20 Maya: yes, for Private deployments we can support no-direct-egress patterns — that'll require a few NAT/firewall configs on your side and we'll coordinate to bake in the correct egress endpoints for model downloads and telemetry.
02:35 Jonas: we care about telemetry — we need traces and token-level metrics forwarded to our prometheus stack. is that possible?
02:43 Maya: we currently push metrics to prometheus-compatible endpoints and also emit traces compatible with open telemetry. one caveat, very small note: some per-token telemetry is sampled to keep cost sensible, we can tune sampling rate for the trial.
03:02 Laura: bridging back to cost — Jonas you mentioned wanting token-level visibility. we can enable per-route token breakdowns in the console and expose csv export for your finance team.
03:15 Jonas: that helps. what's the expected latency floor on Dedicated GPUs? we saw a vendor called LatencyLabs claim sub-50ms — curious what you hit in practice.
03:29 Maya: depends on model and sequence length; for typical 1k-token contexts we see p95 in the 120–200ms range on our current infra for the medium family. if you need sub-50ms you might be looking at a different model/shorter context + highly tuned kernel path; we can run a focused perf run in the trial.
03:51 Aisha: are you able to run benchmarks using our sample prompts? we'd prefer not to leak data into public logs.
04:00 Maya: absolutely — we can run the bench inside your Dedicated pool or Private deployment so the data never leaves your VPC. we'll sign an NDA-ish bench agreement if you like, but in practice it's covered by our trial confidentiality terms.
04:15 Tom: on compliance, we need audit logs for every request and key rotation logs.
04:23 Ravi: audit logs are included in the enterprise package; we can push logs to your cloud logging endpoint (stackdriver). key rotation events can be surfaced via the KMS audit integration. i'll note that as an action item to confirm the exact retention window you need.
04:40 Jonas: timeline — i'd like the trial before the end of q4, ideally ramp in the first two weeks of december. is that doable?
04:48 Laura: yes, if we get the VPC info and IdP details this week we can stand up a Dedicated trial and start the perf bench in the first week of december.
05:00 Aisha: about SSO — we use Okta, SAML 2.0, and we want SCIM user sync later. what's the flow?
05:08 Maya: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. for initial onboarding we'll do SAML for admin access and then enable SCIM once accounts are mapped. please share the Okta metadata file.
05:22 Tom: any known gotchas with SCIM?
05:26 Maya: nothing unusual; sometimes attribute mapping trips folks up (email vs userName). we'll provide a mapping template.
05:36 Jonas: i also want to make sure model routing fallback exists — e.g., if gpu pool is full can requests fallback to a cheaper CPU model?
05:46 Maya: yes, our routing supports policy-based fallback. you can prioritize low-latency or low-cost routes and configure automatic fallback to compatible model variants. we'll go over a routing policy template in the runbook.
06:01 Laura: quick note on support — for the trial you'll have Ravi as the CSM and Maya for engineering support; for production we'll propose a dedicated SLA.
06:12 Jonas: good. any blockers from your side we should know?
06:16 Ravi: primarily we need the following artifacts: 1) VPC peering info + firewall CIDRs, 2) Okta SAML metadata, 3) sample traffic profile (qps, burst patterns, avg seq len), 4) confirmation of retention window for logs. once we have those we'll kick off the Private/Dedicated stub.
06:37 Aisha: i'll compile that — can you provide an example traffic template?
06:42 Maya: yes sending a sample template; also i'll include a short questionnaire about prompt shapes and sensitive PII patterns so we can recommend caching/quantization profiles.
06:57 Jonas: great. last question: any differences in observability for hosted vs private?
07:03 Maya: hosted has built-in console dashboards and downstream integrations; private gives you the option to surface metrics directly to your telemetry stack and we can ship exporter endpoints. also retention policies differ — we can negotiate longer retention for enterprise private customers.
07:24 Tom: okay that's clear.
07:28 Laura: final recap then next steps. recap: we will send the network/VPC diagram, security pack, and onboarding checklist. Maya will schedule the observability walkthrough. Ravi will share Dedicated trial pricing and retention defaults. Pelican will provide Okta metadata, traffic profile, and confirm log retention needs.
07:55 Jonas: sounds good — we'll aim to get the artifacts to you by next tuesday.
08:02 Laura: perfect. thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the links: onboarding doc (link: https://redwood.app/onboarding/pelican-dynamics), security pack (link: https://redwood.app/security/snapshot), and the network diagram template. expect those in your inbox within 48 hours.
08:20 Meeting end.

Notes:
- References to shared artifacts: onboarding doc link above, Dedicated pricing spreadsheet (will be shared), observability sample dashboard (Maya will demo in follow-up).
- Slight transcription noise: a few acronyms mis-heard (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K-V case), vendor name LatencyLabs transcribed as Lattice Labs in one place.

End of transcript.
